title: launchd plist writes identity-daemon logs to a predictable path in shared /tmp
description:
launchd/personal.atwood.persona.plist sets both StandardOutPath and StandardErrorPath to /tmp/personad.log, with RUST_LOG=info.

/tmp is world-writable and the filename is fixed and predictable. Any local user can pre-create /tmp/personad.log as a symlink before the agent first starts and have launchd's file open follow it — launchd does not use O_NOFOLLOW here — giving an arbitrary-file-write/truncate primitive as the daemon's user. If the file is created by launchd with a default mode, another local user can also read personad's logs, which for an identity daemon at info level include the socket path, enumerated identity sources, and attestor probe results.

Use ~/Library/Logs/persona/personad.log (the macOS convention for a LaunchAgent), which is inside the user's home and not attacker-precreatable.

Related install inconsistency worth settling in the same change: the plist runs /usr/local/bin/personad while systemd/personad.service runs %h/.cargo/bin/personad, and no Makefile target installs to either.
close_reason: Fixed together in 67abb54: both stemmed from launchd expanding nothing, so install_service() now substitutes $HOME into a plist template. Binary path is ~/.cargo/bin/personad matching the README and the systemd unit; output is no longer redirected to /tmp and goes to the system log instead. Two tests added.
